author: John Burroughs
title: Wake-Robin
edition: New York: Hurd and Houghton, 1877; the transcribed title page reads “Second Edition, corrected, enlarged, and illustrated”. Prose line wraps are reflowed to spaces; paragraph boundaries and poetry line/stanza breaks are retained. Outer block whitespace, illustration markers, and publisher/digitizer matter are omitted; original transcription punctuation and emphasis conventions are retained. Text follows the Project Gutenberg plain-text file, including its underscore emphasis and double-hyphen dash conventions.

rights.basis: This original English text/edition was published in 1877, before 1931, and its US publication term has expired as of 2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly identifies this transcription as public domain in the USA.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg 35712 plain text (UTF-8) from the PG mirror aleph.pglaf.org. Removed the PG header and footer, producer credits, title-page imprint, copyright leaf, the publishers' note, contents, illustration markers, the page-referenced index and the transcriber's notes; kept the author's preface and the eight chapters. Lines of each paragraph joined with single spaces (indented prose quotations too); multi-line indented verse kept as stanza lines with the block's outer whitespace trimmed and the inner lines' original indentation kept. Chapter titles are level-2 headings under the book title. Burroughs's three footnotes stay where the transcription places them, each after a FOOTNOTES: paragraph label at the end of its essay, in the form [Footnote n: text], with the [n] anchors kept in the running text.
